sources.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations
sources.locator: Complete lecture-note PDF. §4.3, printed pp. 70–74: Theorem 4.15 and its proof, equations 4.14–4.18, and Theorem 4.18; Exercise 42, printed pp. 75–76, for finite-group Yetter–Drinfeld gradings.

contents.name: Finite Drinfeld double cross-relations and Hopf structure in the source convention
contents.reason: Used as a complete independent treatment to check the finite-double construction and index manipulations. The source convention is recorded separately; the local H*op formula is typed and proved from its own definition.

contents.name: Crossing identities and associativity calculation
contents.reason: The source supplied an independent comparison for the crossing calculations; the local proof pairs both distributive laws and expands both associations.

contents.name: Double coproduct, antipode, and canonical R-matrix
Universal R-matrix and its module braiding
contents.reason: The complete source proof was read for independent comparison; the local proof derives the identities from the proved regular-module braiding.

contents.name: Yetter–Drinfeld module action and braided structure
contents.reason: The left-left compatibility and dual action were checked against the source, while the local definition and action proof keep the selected H*op convention explicit.

contents.name: Finite-group double formulas and grading example
contents.reason: The group-basis formulas are rechecked directly from the local normal-order product, coproduct, antipode, R, and coaction equations.

contents.name: Nonabelian group cross-relations and non-flip braiding
contents.reason: The source gives the finite-group double context; the assigned S3 products and basis-tensor braiding are computed directly in the local example.

contents.name: General infinite-dimensional doubles
contents.reason: HH-10 constructs only the finite-dimensional double. The assigned infinite-group item is the row-rank obstruction to a coproduct on the full dual, proved locally.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych, and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories
sources.locator: Complete author PDF. §7.14, pp. 163–165, especially equation 7.46 and Propositions 7.14.6 and 7.14.8; §7.15 for the center/Yetter–Drinfeld braided-category construction.

contents.name: Finite-double modules and the Yetter–Drinfeld compatibility mechanism
contents.reason: Used to cross-check the categorical equivalence and braiding mechanism. The local proof reconstructs the coaction, verifies both directions of the crossing, and checks the tensor and braiding identities.

contents.name: Braided structure on Yetter–Drinfeld modules
contents.reason: The source's categorical treatment was read in full; the local proof checks inverse, linearity, colinearity, naturality, and both hexagons explicitly.

contents.name: Quasitriangular structure and regular-module recovery
contents.reason: The source's monoidal and braiding framework was used as an independent check; the local theorem proves each R identity from the regular modules.

contents.name: Source formulas in a different dual-opposite convention
contents.reason: No formula is copied without convention conversion. HH-10 fixes H*op and the local calculations establish that convention independently.

sources.title: G. A. García and C. Vay, Simple modules of small quantum groups at dihedral groups, Documenta Mathematica 29 (2024)
sources.locator: Complete article PDF. §3.1.3, pp. 5–6: the H*op subalgebra, inverse-crossing relation, canonical R, Yetter–Drinfeld action, and induced braiding.

contents.name: H*op convention and inverse crossing
contents.reason: The exact convention was compared with the local statement. The local proof independently verifies the inverse crossing by finite-dual pairing.

contents.name: Yetter–Drinfeld modules and their braiding
contents.reason: Used as a third independent formula check; the local proof supplies all intermediate action/coaction calculations.

contents.name: Canonical R for a finite double
contents.reason: The source formula was checked against the dual-first normal order and then verified locally from the module hexagons.

contents.name: Nonabelian finite-double cross-relations
contents.reason: The article's explicit double convention was compared with the S3 basis calculation, which is proved directly from the assigned finite-group example.

companions.reason: The finite-group examples use the covered A-page formulas and are checked by direct finite computations. The infinite-group counterexample is a complete local row-rank proof; the sources provide context and do not replace that proof.
